title: Choose the visual world for Glide
question: The roll assigned Race Broadcast. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Race Broadcast
options.lineage: Speedrun race broadcasts (GDQ, race restreams): timer strips and split columns
options.thesis: Your leveling run shown the way a speedrun broadcast shows a race: the route as splits, pace as a live delta.
options.viewport: Cobalt nav rail; a timer strip on top (level, XP bar, XP/hour with its history, time to level, session clock); the current step on the one reversed white plate, the next steps as a split column with modelled time and delta; coach feed, gear, buffs and reminders on the right.
options.risk: Tips into esports flash if the colour bars and motion aren't held back.

raised.raise: State is carried by line form as well as colour: solid live, dashed pending, struck done, so colour is never the only signal.
Exactly one element per screen gets the reversed plate: the current step.
Each quest carries one short code shared by its map pin, its split row and the quest log.
Every pace number carries its proof: XP/hour and time to level show their last 30 minutes.
The split column's header names the span in view: steps 12 to 22, Elwynn Forest.

options.label: Pace Notes
options.thesis: The coach is your co-driver: what's ahead is written as pace notes, distance and direction first.
options.viewport: Graphite shell with a standard side nav; the next three moves as pace-note lines (590 yd NE, Marshal Dughan, Goldshire) on a paper-white panel; pace and gear in a quiet column beside it.
options.risk: The most natural metaphor for a spoken coach, so likely where many runs land; the notebook can turn into a costume.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: Airport departure boards and boarding passes
options.thesis: The route as a departure board: the next stop leads, and a changed waypoint stays lit until you've seen it.
options.viewport: Top bar nav; the next stops as a ranked board (step, place, distance, ETA, status); a boarding-pass card for the current step with its quest codes.
options.case: Holds product clarity (next stop, distance, ETA) but players identify less with airports than with speedrun broadcasts.
options.risk: Reads as a travel app if the game vocabulary isn't on every row.

options.label: Emission-line rail
options.thesis: Every value as a hairline on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with every step as a tick.
options.case: Hairline-only colour fails the arm's-length glance; players don't identify with spectroscopy.
options.kept: State carried by line form, not only hue.

options.label: Monochrome product
options.thesis: Every claim paired with the interface detail that proves it.
options.case: A marketing form on a working screen; no tie to the game.
options.kept: Every number shows its proof (recent history).

options.label: Lexicon page
options.thesis: Guide words name the span you're inside.
options.viewport: A text column with a shoulder index.
options.case: Cream reading page on a dark second monitor mid-session; nothing for the glance.
options.kept: The split column names the span of steps in view.

options.label: Event catalog
options.thesis: Grid and hall map are one space, joined by table codes.
options.viewport: A dense numbered grid keyed to a map.
options.case: Density without hierarchy; the current step would drown.
options.kept: One short code joins a quest's map pin, split row and log entry.

options.label: Timetable rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and reversal.
options.case: One type size can't give the arm's-length glance its scale; raked panes cost legibility.
options.kept: Exactly one reversed plate per screen: the current step.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A modern dark product dashboard (Linear, Raycast), executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Side nav; stat cards on top; step panel, map and coach feed in a grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other dashboard by design.
